slides.headline: Start with the course a learner needs.
slides.speech: Orbit starts with the skill a learner needs, not just the catalog already available. We are developing a request-led course platform connecting learner demand, mentor response and a visible learning journey. This is a prototype with sample screens, not a proven paid service. We are seeking support for a bounded validation cycle.
slides.question: Is the product already live?
slides.answer: Source-visible components and sample-data interfaces exist. A current integrated paid service and learning outcomes are not verified.

slides.headline: A catalog cannot answer every learner's next need.
slides.speech: The founder and friends experienced unmet learning needs. That is the origin of this product, not a representative customer study. Historical MOOC research reported a twelve-point-six percent course-level median completion rate, with wide variation. It is not current Indian dropout data. We will test one practical skill and whether relevant instruction and feedback actually matter to a narrow adult learner group.
slides.question: How many students have this problem?
slides.answer: We have no measured local prevalence. The next sprint is designed to establish that without substituting a published MOOC statistic for our own customers.

panels.title: HISTORICAL CONTEXT, NOT OUR DROPOUT
panels.subtitle: Median completion across 129 reported MOOCs
panels.text: 2015: 129 of 221 collected courses reported completion; range 0.7%-52.1%. Public-data course-level median, no additions after Nov 2013. Not pooled learners, current India or Orbit outcomes.

panels.title: THE LIVED ORIGIN / EVIDENCE LEDGER
panels.text: The exact recent episode and number of friends were not supplied. We will not invent a quote, failed purchase or representative pain score.

panels.title: THREE JOBS TO TEST
panels.text: For proposed learners aged 18+, test relevance, support and practical use separately. A missing catalog item does not automatically mean willingness to pay.

panels.title: TODAY'S ALTERNATIVES
panels.text: Credible alternatives; these limits are hypotheses to test, not competitor findings.

panels.title: PROPOSED DISCOVERY DESIGN
panels.text: Over 14 days, record who, how and when. A convenience sample would remain nonrepresentative; targets are not completed research.

panels.title: THE DECISION, NOT THE HYPE
panels.text: By day 45, stop if fewer than 3 mentors commit or fewer than 10 learners activate. These predeclared thresholds are proposals, not measured demand or approved pilot policy.

slides.headline: Ask for commitment, not compliments.
slides.speech: No one-to-one interviews or primary survey dataset has been supplied. Our proposed fourteen-day sprint targets twelve learner interviews, sixty responses and six mentor conversations. We will test behaviors rather than compliments: a recent unmet skill, a real course request, usable feedback and a mentor's time commitment. Stop rules and sample limits will be stated before collecting results.
slides.question: Do you have validated product-market fit?
slides.answer: No. Personal experience and source work do not establish fit. Written commitments, observed activation and later paid conversion would be stronger evidence.

panels.title: CUSTOMER RESEARCH TODAY
panels.subtitle: One-to-one customer interviews reported
panels.text: No primary survey data supplied. Personal/friends experience is origin, not respondents. Proposed 14 days: 12 learner interviews, 60 adult responses, 6 mentor conversations. No recruitment performed.

panels.text: Unvalidated hypotheses, not commitments.

panels.title: 14-DAY PROPOSED SPRINT
panels.text: Ask about the last task, alternatives, cost, feedback and completion. Survey themes cover topic, urgency, schedule, format, support, price, commitment and consent.

panels.title: EVIDENCE BEFORE A GROWTH CLAIM
panels.text: Waitlists, willingness and completed payments are distinct. No respondent contacts belong in the repository.

panels.title: CHANGE-OUR-MIND RULES
panels.text: Kill criteria are proposed discipline, not certainty. Record contradictions instead of selectively quoting supporters.

panels.title: WHAT CAN BE CLAIMED NEXT
panels.text: Report population, n, date, sampling and missing values. Quotes require permission. Until this happens, customer fit remains unvalidated; secondary studies cannot become our survey.

slides.headline: Demand first. Mentor response. A finite learning path.
slides.speech: The intended loop is request, threshold, signal, build, then learn and rate. Request and vote source exists, but the separate Signal Flare system and richer mentor waves are not one verified lifecycle. The product keeps Student Multiverse, Mentor Dimensions and Peer Space. Finite lessons, feedback and optional mentoring should serve a real skill, not award mastery for animation.
slides.question: What is actually different from a catalog?
slides.answer: The intended demand-to-mentor-production loop is our positioning. It is not proven novel or superior; we must demonstrate it reliably and compare actual customer alternatives.

panels.title: ONE INTENDED REQUEST-TO-LEARNING LOOP
panels.subtitle: Steps to connect demand with useful practice
panels.text: Request, threshold, signal, build, learn + rate. Source requests/votes exist; integrated delivery, stronger waves and course reviews remain unproven. Animation does not establish mastery.

panels.text: Retain 8 Student tiers and 6 Mentor divisions without inventing new names. Selected world redesign and five-or-six-thought destination transitions remain gated intent, not shipped features.

panels.title: WHAT THE LEARNER SHOULD RECEIVE
panels.text: Request support is not a delivery guarantee. Confirm mentor capacity and a realistic launch window; current request and notification lifecycles need integration.

panels.title: FOUR MECHANISMS TO VALIDATE
panels.text: Catalogs, peer help and direct mentors remain credible alternatives; this combination is positioning, not a first-ever claim.

slides.headline: Four screens show interface work—not traction.
slides.speech: We have four inspected sample-data captures from a retained frontend build: lesson journey, course editing, student universe and an idle recorder. External traffic was blocked and no backend or payments were run. The source inventory is substantial, but checkout is unavailable and queued payouts are not bank transfers. Our next milestone is an integrated pilot, not a claim of users or revenue.
slides.question: Can you demonstrate recording and paid completion now?
slides.answer: Not from these captures. The recorder is idle; real media capture, paid checkout, bank settlement and end-to-end learning were not executed.

panels.text: Traction, bank payouts and completion lift are unverified. A 25-payer day-90 target is conditional on commercial clearance; it is not revenue already earned.

slides.headline: One campus and one skill before a national story.
slides.speech: We propose a narrow adult campus pilot, but the first institution, cohort and skill still need founder confirmation. We have no adopted official local enrollment count. The base planning scenario gives nineteen-point-two expected payers from six hundred potential learners, forty percent reach and eight percent conversion. These are synthetic assumptions, not market measurement. Competitor prices provide context, never willingness-to-pay proof.
slides.question: What is your addressable market?
slides.answer: The local relevant cohort is still unknown. We show the bottom-up method and assumption sensitivity, not an unsupported national TAM.

panels.title: BASE PLANNING SCENARIO / NOT A FORECAST
panels.subtitle: Expected payers under synthetic base inputs
panels.text: 600 potential ×40% reach ×8% conversion =19.2 expected payers. Working INR 599 ×12 months gives INR 138,009.60 gross scenario. Fractional expectation is not people acquired; actual cohort count unknown.

panels.text: Neither profile is a verified segment. First campus, city and skill must be selected before local recruitment or population claims.

panels.title: DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE FIRST PILOT
panels.text: Proposed boundaries reduce scope; they do not certify compliance. Test 1 campus, 1 skill and 2 launch cycles before expansion, with professional release review.

panels.text: Official pages observed 16 Nov 2026. Taxes and checkout specifics are not fully established. Different scope/billing means this is not affordability, quality or purchase-intent evidence.

panels.text: All assume INR599 and 12 paid months, not observed retention. Base 19.2 expected payers is independent of the ambitious 25-payer day-90 target. Replace inputs with observed data before forecasting.

slides.headline: Mentor allocation is not platform profit.
slides.speech: Working monthly price points are five ninety-nine and eleven ninety-nine, to be validated. Subscriptions retain twenty percent for the platform and eighty percent for eligible enrolled-course mentors; sessions have a separate fifteen-percent fee. Under an illustrative tax and cost scenario, Core contribution is fifty-point-six-nine rupees. At the modeled tier mix, fifteen thousand fixed monthly cost needs two hundred thirty-seven payers. No actual invoice, tax basis or profit date is claimed.
slides.question: When do you break even?
slides.answer: The model gives237payers only under stated price, mix, usage and cost assumptions. Actual bills, refunds, eligibility and accounting must be validated; there is no promised profit date.

slides.headline: Ninety days should buy two testable launch cycles.
slides.speech: Day one starts only after the owner approves launch. In the first month we target discovery, five mentor commitments, two reviewed courses and thirty learner activations. By day sixty we test one integrated cycle and ten paid learners only if checkout clears. By day ninety we target a second cycle and twenty-five paid learners. If supply or activation is too weak at day forty-five, we stop or redesign.
slides.question: Are these committed outcomes?
slides.answer: No. They are proposed targets with defined gates. Owners and actual start date are unassigned; paid targets remain conditional on commercial release.

panels.text: The INR100,000 proposal is staged across three tranches. At each gate, inspect receipts, usage and evidence. Unspent reserve stays unspent; exact dates and named owners remain unassigned.

slides.headline: Attach people and proof to every milestone.
slides.speech: The founder confirms a team, but names, roles, hours and individual contributions have not been supplied. We will not manufacture a team slide. This page defines the capabilities and proof each milestone needs: engineering, mentor and content quality, customer discovery and commercial release. Source work belongs to the project until individual attribution is confirmed. We also need professional and mentor introductions, not invented advisors.
slides.question: Who on the team can execute this?
slides.answer: Team existence is confirmed, but person-level evidence remains a founder-owned gap. Names, contribution demos and weekly capacity are required before final submission.

slides.headline: INR100,000 to validate—not to assume scale.
slides.speech: Our proposal is one lakh rupees for a ninety-day validation pilot, derived from seven estimated cost lines rather than the two-lakh support ceiling. Forty-five thousand covers recurring infrastructure and support; twenty thousand supports two courses; the rest covers activation, review, testing, a borrowed-first kit and reserve. We also need mentor introductions and pilot access. Quotes, actual cash and funding terms still need confirmation.
slides.question: Why this amount, and what if you receive less?
slides.answer: It is a cost-derived estimate, not an approved budget. Stage45k/35k/20k against evidence; cut kit and activation first, then narrow the second cycle rather than hide a shortfall.
